newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: ICI Pakistan, DuPont seek joint venture.
newsitem.headline: ICI Pakistan, DuPont seek joint venture.

text.p: ICI Pakistan Ltd, a subsidiary of ICI Plc, and the U.S.-based DuPont Co said on Friday they intend to enter into a joint venture to run a pure terephthalic acid (PTA) plant in Karachi.

"ICI Pakistan Limited and E.I. DuPont de Nemours & Company (Inc)., USA, are pleased to announce their intention to enter into a 50-50 joint venture to incorporate ICI Pakistan's PTA plant," a joint statement said.
DuPont on July 14 picked up a 50 percent stake in ICI Pakistan as part of a global deal to buy half of ICI Plc's bulk chemical business for $3 billion.
The very next day ICI Pakistan announced its intention to take a 50 percent stake in the PTA plant which under the global deal goes to DuPont.
ICI Pakistan had said its board of directors was scheduled to consider for approval the proposed joint venture in its meeting on August 12, 1997.
"This proposal is subject to approval by the respective boards and shareholders of ICI Pakistan and DuPont and clearance from all regulatory authorities," the statement said.

ICI Pakistan, listed on the Karachi Stock Exchange with a paid up capital of 7.871 billion rupees ($193.77 million), is currently owned 61 percent by ICI Plc. It manufactures polyester staple fibre, soda ash, paints, pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, explosives, some consumer items and other speciality chemicals.

ICI had planned to start commercial production at its $450 million PTA plant being constructed near Karachi's Port Qasim by November 1997. The plant will manufacture 400,000 tonnes of PTA, a raw material used in making polyster staple fibre, to be sold in Pakistan and abroad.
"This joint venture is based on a recognition of ICI Pakistan's in-market strength and DuPont's world leadership in manufacturing excellence.
"It equally recognises the transfer of (the) PTA technology base to DuPont, consequent to DuPont's acquisition of ICI's PTA global business outside Pakistan," the statement said.
ICI Pakistan's 10-rupee shared have been rising since the announcement of the global deal last week and closed 1.75 rupees higher at 30.40 rupees on Thursday.
